title: Statistics and Further Measures on High-rise Littering
what_it_is: Statistics and Further Measures on High-rise Littering

sections.label: NEA littering reports 2018
sections.summary: NEA received about 26,000 littering reports and 2,700 bulky item disposal reports in public places in 2018.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: The National Environment Agency (NEA) received about 26,000 and 2,700 reports of littering and indiscriminate disposal of bulky items in public places respectively in 2018.

sections.label: NEA enforcement and high-rise reports
sections.summary: In 2018 NEA took about 39,000 littering enforcement actions and 30 for bulky items, with over 7,700 high-rise littering reports from 2016 to 2018.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: In 2018, NEA took about 39,000 enforcement actions against littering in public places, and another 30 for the unlawful disposal of bulky items in public places.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: To the Members' questions on high-rise littering in particular, more than 7,700 reports of such offences were made to NEA between 2016 and 2018.

sections.label: High-rise littering offenders caught
sections.summary: Between August 2012 and December 2018, over 2,200 offenders were caught for high-rise littering, including 52 repeat offenders.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: Between August 2012 and December 2018, more than 2,200 offenders were caught for high-rise littering, of whom 52 were repeat offenders.

sections.label: Penalties for repeat high-rise littering
sections.summary: The fine for repeat high-rise littering offenders for the third and subsequent offence is $10,000 per enforcement action upon conviction.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: As I have said, there are very stiff penalties for high-rise littering and the fine for repeat offenders for the third and subsequent offence is $10,000 per enforcement action upon conviction.

sections.label: Littering reports and enforcement prioritisation
sections.summary: About 26,000 littering reports are received yearly, and NEA prioritises based on offence severity and litter type, with enforcement taking at least 10 weeks.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: In particular, for littering, we receive about 26,000 reports of such incidents per year.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: So, we do prioritise based on the severity of the littering offence, the type of litter and so on, to take action and investigate.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: I said enforcement action takes at least 10 weeks in general.

sections.label: Enforcement proceedings timeline
sections.summary: If there is firm evidence, initiating enforcement proceedings takes another three to five weeks.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: After that, if there is firm evidence, we need to initiate the enforcement proceedings and that takes another three to five weeks.

sections.label: CCTV littering enforcement at Khatib
sections.summary: At MPC@Khatib, CCTV cameras were installed for littering but not viewed until NEA was asked, and five faces were identified.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: At the Multi-Purpose Court (MPC)@Khatib, because of lots of littering, there were closed-circuit television (CCTV) cameras installed but there was no viewing.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Only when I told NEA, "Why don't you view the CCTV?", that they viewed the CCTVs and managed to put five faces and tried to catch them.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: So, I would like to ask if NEA is reviewing its enforcement process and how to be more proactive and diligent in carrying out enforcement.

sections.label: Rise in enforcement actions
sections.summary: Successful enforcement actions rose from about 10 in 2011 to more than 1,200 in 2018.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: If they are willing to come forward to give statements, is NEA willing to take enforcement action?

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: Since then, the number of successful enforcement actions has increased about 120 times.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: So, in 2011, the number of successful enforcement actions was about 10.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: Last year, in 2018, it was more than 1,200.

sections.label: Publicity materials and high-rise littering
sections.summary: MSO produced new publicity materials including standees, and cases in the area fell from 21 to about nine in six months.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: MSO actually came up with a whole new set of publicity materials, including standees, to raise awareness about the issue, too, and also to inform the residents about the number of people caught in that area for high-rise littering together, of course, with active enforcement.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: That has improved the situation in that area significantly, in fact, from 21 cases in the previous six months to about nine cases.

sections.label: Smaller cameras to catch litterers
sections.summary: The speaker suggests making cameras smaller so more people can be caught without waiting for a resident to reach menopause.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Make them smaller so that people cannot see them and then we might be able to catch more people and we do not need to wait for the resident to reach menopause.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: It is not that we did not catch anyone.

sections.label: Deterrent effect and better cameras
sections.summary: Seeing a camera and stopping littering is a good enough deterrent, and better technologies including smaller, more effective cameras are being sought.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: If he sees the camera and he stops littering, that is a good enough deterrent effect.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: We do continue to look out for better technologies which are suitable for investigating our high-rise littering incidences, including, of course, cameras, whether it is smaller cameras, more effective cameras in terms of image resolution, detection capabilities, better video analytics programme, we are doing that.

sections.label: Five-day CCTV deployment cycle
sections.summary: The speaker questions the five-day CCTV deployment cycle, asking who has menstruation in five-day cycles.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah
sentences.text: Next, if CCTV is deployed many times because it is a five-day cycle, who has menstruation in five-day cycles?

sections.label: Litter DNA on ground
sections.summary: When litter falls to the ground, it is unlikely that only the culprit's DNA will be present there.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: First of all, when the litter comes down onto the ground, it is unlikely it is the DNA of the culprit alone that will be there.
